chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him).
That he used to grant inheritance to the Magian if he married his mother and his daughter through two aspects: from the aspect that she is his mother, and from the aspect that she is his wife.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: Our companions, may God have mercy on them, differed regarding the inheritance of the Magian if he married one of the prohibited relatives by lineage according to Islamic law. Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman and many of the later followers said: He inherits only from the lineage and the cause that are permissible in Islamic law. As for what is not permissible in Islamic law, he does not inherit from it under any circumstance.

And al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and some of the later followers who followed him said on his opinion: He inherits from the lineage under all circumstances, even if it was acquired through a cause that is not permissible in Islamic law. As for the cause, he inherits from it only through what is permissible in Islamic law.
And the correct opinion in my view is that the Magian inherits from both lineage and cause together, whether they are permissible in Islamic law or not.

And that which indicates this is the report we mentioned earlier from al-Sakuni, and what our companions mentioned in opposition to it is not supported by a trace from the Infallibles (peace be upon them), nor is there evidence for it from the apparent text of the Quran.
But they said it only as a form of consideration, and that is discarded among us by consensus.

And furthermore, these lineages and causes, although they are not permissible in Islamic law, are permissible among them, and they believe that it is through that which the private parts are made lawful, and they are not made lawful by anything else. So it runs the course of the contract in Islamic law.
ai.seo_question: Does a Magian inherit from a relative if he married her in a way that is prohibited in Islamic law but valid in his own religion?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic debate among Shia scholars regarding whether a Magian inherits through lineage (*nasab*) and marriage (*sabab*) even when the specific bond is prohibited in Islamic law but valid in their own religion. Shaykh al-Tusi affirms the view that inheritance applies to both causes, arguing that since the Magian considers the prohibited union a valid contract for lawful relations, it functions analogously to a proper Islamic marriage for inheritance purposes. This ruling underscores the principle of *al-ijtihad bi-l-ra'y* (independent reasoning) in applying Islamic legal concepts to non-Muslims based on their internal religious validity.
